Mastering System Consolidation: Evidence-Backed Integration of 3tched and threetched

flag
Introduction
What if over half of your custom microservice API surface wasn't actually performing any unique business logic, but merely wrapping command-line calls to an underlying runtime engine? In complex software architectures, redundant abstraction layers accumulate quickly, masking true system responsibilities and burdening developers with duplicate schema definitions.
In this evidence-backed architectural lesson, we examine the system consolidation of /srv/git/odbus-verified. You will master how to audit overlapping plugin functionality, bridge native schema capture gaps, and establish a bulletproof boundary between native engine contracts and local system integrations. By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
  • Differentiate precisely between our local filesystem/project engine (3tched) and the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime (threetched).
  • Audit all 74 plugins and 1,388 methods across mounted namespaces to classify exact duplicates, partial overlaps, and distinct responsibilities.
  • Analyze critical native capture gaps in HTTP routes, WebSocket generation frames, tool parameter domains, and structured receipts.
  • Formulate a phased, zero-risk migration dependency map that offloads redundant handwritten declarations into native threetched contracts without disrupting caller state or capability enforcement.
Architecture & Mounted Inventory: 3tched vs. threetched
To understand consolidation, we must first establish the foundational identity invariant governing our codebase: the container is the identity, and 3tchedFS is its lungs. However, historical naming drift created confusion between our internal code and external runtimes. Let's fix that mental model right now with the official owner-directed naming distinction:
  • 3tched: Refers exclusively to our code—the local, typed filesystem interface and project engine (Cargo package tched-fs, plugin tched_fs, retained source directory crates/threetched-fs).
  • threetched: Refers to the external ZeroClaw-derived runtime and surface, backed directly by the autonomous binary at /usr/bin/threetched (built from vendor/tched-router/source.pin at upstream commit a56c345d51dd8ab562e9351e0d4ab83f6a741db9).
When we inspect our running server host, the FUSE engine projects two separate host views under /run/mounts/:
  1. /run/mounts/3tchedFS: Exposes our 70 OP-DBUS plugins (1,180 total methods), representing our custom filesystem, state, and identity interfaces.
  2. /run/mounts/threetched: Exposes the 4 upstream plugins (threetched with 147 methods, tched_router with 43 methods, tched_plugins with 6 methods, and tched_skills with 12 methods).
Together, these two mounted views form a disjoint union of exactly 74 catalog plugins and 1,388 method declarations (catalog generation 74, catalog hash 8a34d0da9517b137063314e07f5fa9a24fe3a3fe33920b1de2df941380041fd6).
Another load-bearing invariant is that the plugin IS the schema, and the sealed blob IS the plugin. Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog at /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob. Crucially, moving duplicate declarations into another handwritten plugin (such as large_language_model) is not consolidation—it merely moves the duplication around! Functionality owned by threetched must derive directly from its native captured binary contract at seal time.
Plugin & Method Decision Matrix
To systematically clean up our codebase, we evaluate all 74 mounted plugins against their underlying implementations. We categorize every plugin into one of four concrete disposition tiers:
1. Confirmed Wrappers (To Collapse Immediately)
These are pure handwritten wrappers that duplicate native threetched operations one-for-one. They can be safely deleted once callers rebind directly to threetched:
  • tched_plugins (6 methods): Direct wrapper around plugin.install, list, migrate, info, remove, search (source: crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/tched_plugins.rs).
  • tched_skills (12 methods): Direct wrapper around skills.add, audit, edit, install, list, remove, test, and skills.bundle.* (source: crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/tched_skills.rs).
  • large_language_model (8 methods): Facade over native Chat, GetState, ListModels, ListProviders, and SetProvider (source: crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/large_language_model_methods.rs:44).
  • gemma_brain.route (1 method): Facade calling tched_router.ResolveRoute.
  • model_registry.native_list_providers (1 method): Simple wrapper over native providers.list.
2. Mixed / Partial Overlaps (To Consolidate After Capture)
These plugins combine native binary features with local bridge logic:
  • tched_router (43 methods): Blends native config/model routes with local job bookkeeping, committed SHM state, and session admission.
  • cron (9 methods): 7 methods map to native CLI actions (cron.add, cron.list, cron.update, etc.), while 2 (get_history, run_job) require native HTTP endpoint capture.
  • mcp (3 methods): 2 methods are native config facades (GetMcpConfig, PatchConfig), while configure_tool_groups is local bridge projection policy.
  • cognitive (670 methods): Contains 567 persona methods and 1 specialist that share the native threetched completion backend (agent/agents.*).
3. Different Responsibilities (Genuinely Ours)
These plugins represent our unique intellectual property and core infrastructure. They must remain in 3tched:
  • tched_fs: Our typed filesystem protocol and receipt contract (cap.storage.3tchedfs.*).
  • identity_sled: Container identity, physical-root migration, and credential lifecycle.
  • project: Container-backed project ACLs, document ownership, and session context.
  • btrfs, cozo, qdrant, snowball: Storage, vector index, graph state, and audit stream management.
  • freedesktop, incus, openflow, ovsdb_bridge, elevation: System supervision, networking, and security elevation.
4. Unestablished / Domain-Specific
Specialized external integrations requiring further evidence before any refactoring: notebooklm (47 methods), emqx (12 methods), dnsresolver (20 methods), xray (4 methods), wgcf (8 methods).

Native Capture Gap Analysis & Pipeline Ingestion
Why can't we just delete all 43 methods of tched_router today? Because the earlier mapping report made a critical assumption: it treated CLI help capture as proof of complete operation equivalence. In reality, there is a massive contract gap between CLI invocation and typed domain APIs!
The current native capture format (threetched-cli/1, config schema SHA-256 a98561f7b8c9f6a1be529557afc1bf123fee566958363cee211c998a5cb34cef) captures CLI flags and top-level TOML schemas. However, every CLI command in threetched currently declares an identical return shape: {stdout: String, stderr: String, exit: i32} with idempotent=false. Compare that to our handwritten OP-DBUS methods, which return structured JSON objects, deterministic state receipts (operation_id, result_digest), and granular error variants!
To achieve true consolidation without losing functionality, we must capture five missing native contract categories directly from the threetched binary during seal time:
  1. Typed Native HTTP APIs: Native endpoints like /cron/history, /cron/run, /api/tools, and /agents expose rich JSON responses that are completely absent from CLI help flags.
  2. Tool Schemas & param_domains: Native agent tools define parameter domain restrictions that must be ingested into PluginSchema tool definitions.
  3. WebSocket Generation Frames & Cancellation: Real-time generation (/ws/chat) and out-of-band cancellation (cancel_generation) rely on WebSocket frame protocols rather than synchronous CLI calls.
  4. Structured Receipts & Idempotency: Handwritten methods provide atomic SHM state commits and idempotency guarantees that stdout strings cannot supply.
  5. Identity & Scope Enforcement: CLI execution uses the ambient environment; native contracts must be bound to caller identity headers (SID1/OIA1).
How to Ingest Gaps Without Secondary Schema Authorities
We must never create a parallel schemas/ directory or hand-edited JSON files. Instead, we enhance the binary capture builder (vendor/tched-router/build-threetched.sh and crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/threetched.rs). On every seal run (opblob seal-shm), the sealer executes the verified threetched binary, inspects its embedded OpenAPI specification and tool manifests, and automatically populates the native threetched PluginSchema. This keeps schema authority 100% inside the sealed blob!
Cognitive Deep-Dive & Configuration Offloading
The cognitive plugin is by far the largest surface in our catalog, declaring 670 methods. However, when we inspect its source implementation (crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/specialist.rs:383), we discover a striking truth: over 85% of these methods are repetitive persona prompts sharing a single inference backend!
Let's break down the 670 cognitive methods into functional categories:
  • Persona Consultations (567 methods): 81 distinct personas (e.g., agent_dbus_expert, agent_rust_pro, agent_fedramp) multiplied by 7 action verbs (advise, analyze, consult, explain, help, recommend, review). Every single one of these formats a prompt and forwards it to the native threetched completion backend.
  • Execution Catalog (59 methods): 12 exposed aliases across 5 language execution engines (Rust, Python, JS/TS, Go, shell). These map functionally to native /shell_tool, runtime profiles, and agent execution tools.
  • Orchestration Catalog (18 methods): 6 agents x 3 operations (code-review-orchestrator, context-manager, dx-optimizer, memory, sequential-thinking, tdd-orchestrator). These map to native SOP and pipeline tools.
  • Memory & Code Retrieval (10 methods): memory_store, memory_query, code_search, code_index. These overlap native /memory and /project_intel endpoints while preserving Voyage-4 collection bindings.
  • Discovery, Admission & Policy (6 methods): get_health, list_tools, invoke_tool, schema_read, oscal_subids, toolsets. Essential local bridge enforcement.
The Offloading Strategy
Instead of maintaining 567 separately authored Rust schema methods for persona consultations, we can represent these personas as native TOML configuration sections under [agents.<alias>] in /etc/op-dbus/threetched-runtime.toml!
When a user invokes a persona consultation, the threetched engine resolves the agent alias from its native configuration, loads the system prompt, and executes inference through its native provider drivers. This eliminates 567 handwritten methods from cognitive in one fell swoop, while preserving exact persona prompt behavior!
Migration Dependency Map & Capability Realignment
A system consolidation is only as safe as its dependency map. Before we delete a single line of wrapper code, we must trace how callers, state stores, capabilities, and UI components interact across the entire stack.
1. UI & Frontend Callers
Our production UI is a SvelteKit chat app (/srv/git/3tched.com) communicating via gRPC-Web over port :8090. Currently, the UI issues calls to tched_router.Chat, large_language_model.generate, and gemma_brain.route. When consolidating, the UI door adapter (src/grpc/door.ts) must be re-pointed to invoke threetched.Chat or native provider interfaces, carrying the unchanged identity metadata (SID1/OIA1).
2. Bridge State Engine & MutationEngine
crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/mutation_engine.rs folds authoritative backend results into canonical SHM state. When tched_plugins, tched_skills, and tched_router are collapsed, MutationEngine's private result handlers must be updated to commit state changes directly under the unified threetched plugin ID.
3. Capability Mappings
Handwritten methods use explicit capabilities like cap.software.3tched-router.chat@v1. Native threetched CLI methods use command-specific hashed capabilities like cap.software.threetched.call.ccc2ba7f9b4187...@v1. The capability materializer (op-grants-materializer) must update /etc/op-dbus/capability-grants.json` so active session principals retain uninterrupted access.
4. Filesystem Projection (3tchedFS)
The FUSE engine (crates/threetched-fs/src/namespace.rs) projects sealed plugin schemas as directory trees under /run/mounts/3tchedFS/plugins/. Collapsing duplicate wrappers reduces filesystem node inflation while leaving our core filesystem contract (tched_fs) fully intact.

End-to-End Migration & Dataflow Pipeline

Phased Execution Sequence & Evidence Appendix
To execute this consolidation with zero downtime and complete auditability, we follow a strict five-phase sequence. Each phase requires explicit evidence gates before proceeding to the next:
Phase 1: Native Capture Enhancement
   └─► Phase 2: Collapse Direct Wrappers (tched_plugins, tched_skills)
          └─► Phase 3: Offload Persona Configurations (567 methods)
                 └─► Phase 4: Consolidate Router & LLM Facades
                        └─► Phase 5: Reseal Blob Catalog & Deploy Release
Phase Details & Verification Evidence
  1. Phase 1 (Native Capture Enhancement): Update crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/threetched.rs to capture native OpenAPI endpoints, WS frames, and tool param_domains during build. Gate: Verify native capture schema includes HTTP/WS contracts.
  2. Phase 2 (Collapse Direct Wrappers): Delete crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/tched_plugins.rs and tched_skills.rs. Re-route callers to threetched. Gate: cargo check --workspace passes clean.
  3. Phase 3 (Offload Persona Configurations): Generate TOML [agents.<alias>] definitions for 81 personas. Remove 567 persona methods from cognitive. Gate: Persona inference test returns valid completions via native agent resolver.
  4. Phase 4 (Consolidate Router & LLM Facades): Rebind large_language_model and tched_router callers to threetched. Update MutationEngine state dispatch. Gate: Chat turns execute with valid operation_id receipts.
  5. Phase 5 (Reseal & Activation): Run opblob seal-shm, execute ./activate-golden.sh, and verify active release status. Gate: /run/mounts/3tchedFS and /run/mounts/threetched report zero missing plugin errors.
Three Immediate Next Actions (Read-Only Planning)
To resolve the remaining capture gaps without modifying code, the next three actions are:
  • Action 1: Execute a read-only capture of the running threetched binary's native OpenAPI spec to map typed HTTP return schemas (resolves Gap 1).
  • Action 2: Benchmark native tool parameter domains (param_domains) against handwritten tool input schemas in cognitive (resolves Gap 2).
  • Action 3: Draft a native [agents] TOML translation file for the 81 persona prompt definitions to validate config offloading (resolves Gap 3).

Summary
By cleanly separating our custom filesystem engine (3tched) from the ZeroClaw-derived runtime (threetched), we eliminate over 600 redundant wrapper methods, eliminate dual schema authorities, and preserve critical identity and state guarantees.
Key Takeaways
  • Identity Distinction: 3tched identifies our local Rust code (tched-fs, tched_fs); threetched identifies the external ZeroClaw runtime binary.
  • Single Schema Authority: The sealed blob IS the plugin. Functionality owned by threetched must derive directly from its native captured contract, never from secondary schemas/ directories or handwritten wrapper plugins.
  • Capture Gap Resolution: Before deleting wrappers, native capture must ingest OpenAPI HTTP routes, WebSocket generation frames, and tool param_domains to preserve typed domain result contracts.
  • Cognitive Offloading: 567 persona consultation methods can be cleanly offloaded into native [agents.<alias>] TOML configuration sections, dramatically simplifying our codebase.
